speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing a psychiatric condition along with a new onset movement disorder. To help me understand your situation, how long have these symptoms been present, and can you describe specifically what kind of movements you are experiencing?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is excellent news regarding your schizophrenia symptoms. However, the movement disorder you mentioned is likely a side effect from the risperidone we started two months ago. Can you describe exactly what movements are happening—are they involuntary, repetitive, or perhaps stiffness or tremors?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those symptoms—persistent restlessness, fidgeting, and pacing—are classic signs of akathisia. This is a common side effect of the risperidone you started two months ago. Have you noticed any worsening of these feelings recently, or have they been constant since beginning the medication?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced akathisia secondary to risperidone.

The symptoms you describe—inner restlessness, fidgeting, and an inability to remain still—are classic signs of this medication side effect. Given your history of starting risperidone two months ago, I am confident in this diagnosis without further testing. Would you like to discuss management options to alleviate these distressing symptoms?
